newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ Australian job ads fall 7.3 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ Australian job ads fall 7.3 pct in May.

text.p: The Australian and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group Ltd said on Tuesday its job advertisement series fell an adjusted 7.3 percent in May following a 16.7 percent rise in April.
"The fall in the number of job ads in May is best interpreted as payback for the artificially large increase recorded in April," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said.
He said April's record increase was inflated by the failure of the seasonal adjustement to correct for an early Easter.
"A more sensible way to read the data is to note that the number of job ads in the three months ended May was 8.6 percent higher than the preceding three months," he said.
This compared with a 0.4 percent increase in the three months ended February and a 3.3 percent decline in the three months to end November, Eslake added.
Seasonally adjusted job ads were up 2.2 percent on the year in May while the trend series rose 2.1 percent in the month to be 4.2 percent higher than a year ago.

The trend in job advertising over the past few months was consistent with net new job creation averaging around 14,000 per month over the next three months, an improvement on the 6,100 per month recorded over the first four months of 1997, Eslake said.

"The pace of net new job creation would then need to step up to an average of around 19,000 per month between August and June 1998 to meet the government's Budget forecast of two percent employment growth in 1997/98 as a whole," he said.

"This appears to be a plausible scenario given the widespread expectation of an acceleration in economic growth over the coming financial year as the effects of the decline in interest rates over the past twelve months work their way through," Eslake said.
Job ads fell in all states except Victoria where they were unchanged, with the biggest falls in the ACT and New South Wales.
